samples.summary: New `YorkieStore.applyMerge` budget guard (the CRDT write path for every merge in the editor) has no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff rewrites `setMerge` for both the batched (paste) and unbatched paths through a new private `applyMerge` that silently `return`s (dropping the merge) when `mergeBudgetAdmits(mergeBudgetOf(Object.values(ws.merges)), [span])` is false. No frontend test touches it: `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/*.test.ts` are csv/image tests only, and `packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet/` (yorkie-axis-order, yorkie-cut-paste, yorkie-store-read-only, remote-change-utils) never call `setMerge` or assert on `merges` (only a path string in remote-change-utils.test.ts:18). If this guard is wrong — e.g. the `!ws.merges[sref]` pre-condition or the budget recomputation misbehaves — a user's merge is silently dropped with no error, and nothing in the suite would catch it. The sheets-side tests exercise `Sheet`/`MemStore`, not this store.

samples.summary: XLSX importer's new merge-budget skip is untested; only a single-merge happy path exists
samples.evidence: `applyMergeRanges` now accumulates a budget and `continue`s past merges that exceed it, silently importing a file without some of its merged blocks. The only merge coverage in `packages/sheets/test/import/xlsx-importer.test.ts` is one `<mergeCell ref="A1:B1"/>` asserted at line 103. No test builds a workbook that exceeds `MaxMergeEntries`/`MaxMergeCoveredCells`, so an off-by-one or wrong accumulation (e.g. counting an over-budget span anyway, or aborting the whole loop) would ship unnoticed as silently lost layout on import.

samples.summary: `applyPasteMerges` budget-drop branch (paste silently dropping over-budget merged blocks) has no test
samples.evidence: The diff adds `if (!mergeBudgetAdmits(budget, [merge.span])) continue;` inside `applyPasteMerges`, described as the gesture where the budget is 'most easily overspent'. The new `Sheet merge + copy-paste` block in packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts covers re-creation, cut drops, partial-overwrite refusal and freeze refusal, but no case where the paste exceeds the budget; the only budget tests (merge.test.ts:16-55) call `mergeBudgetError`/`mergeBudgetAdmits` directly and `canMergeSelection`/`mergeSelection`. A wrong accumulation here would silently drop pasted merges (or store a map the next load cannot walk).
searchedFor: Read merge.test.ts new copy-paste describe block

samples.summary: `sortFilterByColumn` clearing the copy buffer is untested
samples.evidence: The diff adds `this.clearCopyBuffer()` to `sortFilterByColumn` on the same rationale as `shiftCells`/`moveCells`, and both of those got explicit tests (merge.test.ts:157, :174). No filter test asserts the buffer state: packages/sheets/test/sheet/filter.test.ts calls `sortFilterByColumn` at lines 203, 226, 260, 325 without any `getCopyRange()` assertion, and `getCopyRange` appears only in merge.test.ts and clipboard.test.ts. If the call were removed, a post-sort paste would relocate from stale coordinates with nothing failing.

samples.summary: View-layer changes (drag-reorder `if (!moved) return`, and the two paste handlers no longer clearing the copy buffer) have no test
samples.evidence: `moveRows`/`moveColumns` returning a boolean is covered at the model level (merge.test.ts:1197-1198), but the consumer change in `Worksheet`'s drag-reorder handler — skipping the selection update on a refused reorder — is asserted nowhere; likewise the removal of `clearCopyBuffer()` in `Worksheet.paste` (worksheet.ts:~4950) and `Spreadsheet.paste` (spreadsheet.ts:724). The repeat-paste behavior is proved only through `Sheet.paste` directly (merge.test.ts 'should propagate merges on a second paste from the same copy'), which bypasses the view code that used to clear the buffer. I searched packages/sheets/test/view/* (worksheet-mouse, worksheet-keymap, gridcanvas) and found no moveRows/paste-buffer assertions.

samples.summary: `snapshotMergesIn`'s exclusion of partially-clipped merged blocks is untested
samples.evidence: The new helper filters copied merges to those fully inside the copied range (`isRangeInRange`). Every new copy-paste test in merge.test.ts selects ranges that either contain the block whole or contain none, so the filter branch never fires; removing the `.filter(...)` would leave the suite green while a clipped block got re-created at the destination with a span that overflows the pasted region.
searchedFor: reviewed the new 'Sheet merge + copy-paste' tests in merge.test.ts

samples.summary: Backend freeze-related merge checks are tested only on one axis each
samples.evidence: `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` reads both `frozenRows` and `frozenCols`, but worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts only adds row-axis cases ('refuses a move that would park a merged block across the freeze' / 'allows a move…'); no column-axis move against `frozenCols` is exercised. Similarly worksheet.controller.spec.ts's new `setFreeze` snap test passes `{rows: 2, cols: 0}` only, so the `frozenCols` sweep of `snapFreezePastMerges` through the API is uncovered (the sheets-level column case is covered in merge.test.ts, but not the controller wiring). A column-axis wiring mistake would ship undetected.
searchedFor: read new specs in worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts and worksheet.controller.spec.ts

samples.summary: `canMergeSelection`'s entry-count cap (`MaxMergeEntries`) is never exercised through the Sheet
samples.evidence: 'refuses a selection the budget cannot afford' only builds a selection whose single span exceeds `MaxMergedCells`; the count and covered-cells caps are checked only against the pure `mergeBudgetError`/`mergeBudgetAdmits` functions. So the wiring of `this.mergeBudget` (maintained in `rebuildMergeCoverMap`) into `canMergeSelection` is untested for the cases the budget field actually matters — if `mergeBudget` were never updated, the per-span branch would still return false and this test would still pass.
searchedFor: read merge budget describe block in merge.test.ts

samples.summary: Tautological assertion inside the merge-budget test
samples.evidence: `expect(budget.coveredCells + MaxMergedCells).toBeGreaterThan(MaxMergeCoveredCells)` is arithmetic over two exported constants and a locally constructed object; it holds regardless of any behavior in `merging.ts` beyond the constants' values. It documents the setup rather than testing anything — harmless, but it inflates the appearance of coverage in that test.

Three new `RangeOpRefusal` variants ('merge-paste-partial', 'merge-paste-frozen', 'merge-move-frozen') gain user-facing strings in `refusalMessage`; tests assert only the refusal codes (merge.test.ts:585, 668, 704, 801, 992, 1133), never the rendered message. Low impact (a wrong string is cosmetic and the switch is exhaustive under tsc).

finding.summary: New `YorkieStore.applyMerge` budget guard (the CRDT write path for every merge in the editor) has no test at all
finding.evidence: The diff rewrites `setMerge` for both the batched (paste) and unbatched paths through a new private `applyMerge` that silently `return`s (dropping the merge) when `mergeBudgetAdmits(mergeBudgetOf(Object.values(ws.merges)), [span])` is false. No frontend test touches it: `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/*.test.ts` are csv/image tests only, and `packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet/` (yorkie-axis-order, yorkie-cut-paste, yorkie-store-read-only, remote-change-utils) never call `setMerge` or assert on `merges` (only a path string in remote-change-utils.test.ts:18). verdict.reason: The code exists as described: YorkieStore.applyMerge (yorkie-store.ts:977-994) silently returns, dropping the merge, when `!ws.merges[sref] && !mergeBudgetAdmits(mergeBudgetOf(Object.values(ws.merges)), [span])`, and setMerge (yorkie-store.ts:996-1009) routes both the batched paste path and the unbatched path through it. I searched for a counterexample well beyond the reviewer's paths: repo-wide greps for `applyMerge|mergeBudgetAdmits|mergeBudgetOf` and `setMerge` return only sheets tests over Sheet/MemStore (packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:8-38, 887, 913, 929), backend controller specs, and a CLI test — never YorkieStore. A case-insensitive `merge` grep across ALL of packages/frontend (src and tests, not just tests/app/spreadsheet) shows no spreadsheet yorkie test mentioning merge at all, including the files the reviewer did not enumerate (yorkie-concurrency.test.ts, yorkie-concurrency-repro.test.ts, yorkie-cross-sheet.integration.ts, yorkie-worksheet-comments.test.ts). Grep for `yorkie-store|YorkieStore` shows the only test consumers are yorkie-axis-order, yorkie-cut-paste and yorkie-store-read-only; I read yorkie-store-read-only.test.ts in full (lines 88-197) and it covers only presence seeding, ensureAxisOrder and comment-thread gates, with no generic iteration over write methods. The only other frontend setMerge caller is the visual harness sheet-scenarios.tsx:230, which uses MemStore. No e2e coverage exists (`**/e2e/**` grep for merge: none). Blocking under this lens: a changed behavior on the CRDT write path for every editor merge, whose failure silently discards a user's merge with no error, has no meaningful test — a data-affecting, user-visible gap (major).
